title: No server-side maxObjectsInGet enforcement
description: Found while verifying the maxObjectsInSet report. No *-server crate enforces maxObjectsInGet (grep max_objects_in_get / maxObjectsInGet in crate-*-server/src: no hits), although clients document it and consumers advertise it in the Session. RFC 8620 §5.1 (rfc8620.txt L1663): '"requestTooLarge": The number of ids requested by the client exceeds the maximum number the server is willing to process in a single method call.' Consider a helper mirroring enforce_max_objects_in_set that returns method-level requestTooLarge, wired into the generic /get handler. Decide whether the library should enforce it or leave it to consumers.
notes:
Mark 2026-10-19: library enforces maxObjectsInGet in the generic /get path with method-level requestTooLarge (RFC 8620 5.1), mirroring the .30 /set fix.
Regression test (attempt 1): crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs tests handle_get_over_max_objects_is_request_too_large (501 ids vs default cap, FAILS at HEAD: handle_get returns 501 notFound instead of requestTooLarge) and handle_get_null_ids_is_not_counted_against_cap (passes; null ids not counted, RFC 8620 L1663 counts ids requested). Test assumes default max_objects_in_get = 500 (RFC 8620 L546-547 suggested minimum, mirrors max_objects_in_set default).
Fix (uncommitted): JmapBackend::max_objects_in_get (default 500, mirrors max_objects_in_set) + jmap_server::enforce_max_objects_in_get(args, max) -> method-level requestTooLarge, description maxObjectsInGet. Wired into handle_get and 16 custom /get handlers (chat: ban, invite, presence, contact, space, message, position, emoji; mail: vacation, submission, thread, email, mailbox, identity, sieve; calendars: event). null/absent ids count as 0. SearchSnippet/get emailIds split to JMAP-yt1w.38. fmt/clippy/test/doc gates green.
Done in 3498a6f4: tests handlers::tests::handle_get_over_max_objects_is_request_too_large, handlers::tests::handle_get_null_ids_is_not_counted_against_cap; changed existing tests: none
